findings.title: Benchmark steps can't separate the two interventions, so the baseline can't be reproduced
findings.description:
Step 3 lists four bench runs labelled "counter-gating" or "break enabled". Runs 1 and 2 use the same command (`--subdivision-factor 1`), and so do runs 3 and 4 (`--subdivision-factor 3`). The design never adds a way to switch early exit on or off. Intervention 1 replaces counter-gating outright (line 25). Once it ships, the run labelled "Baseline … should reproduce slice 145 ~38 TPS" will actually run with early exit on. As a result:
- A2 ("≥5× vs slice 145 baseline") has to be compared against the historical 38 TPS figure, not a fresh run.
- The per-intervention attribution that line 58 says "needs CUDA measurement" can't be measured.

Pick one fix. Either add a bench-only switch (a kernel template constant, not a runtime branch), or drop the attribution runs. If you drop them, state that the baseline is the recorded slice 145 figure and keep only the S=1 and S=3 runs.

findings.title: `cell_size` and `S` are separate settings that can disagree
findings.description:
The component diagram stores `cell_size` and `subdivision_factor S` as two separate `BenchConfig` fields. Both are passed to the kernel. Line 80 says the harness "reads [cell_size] from config", but `cell_size = query_radius / S` is only valid if `cell_size` is calculated from `S`. If they are set separately:
- `cell_size < query_radius / S` makes the ±S scan too small. Neighbors inside the radius are silently missed.
- `cell_size > query_radius / S` scans more cells than needed.

The validation block (lines 69–76) checks only `S`. State that `cell_size` is calculated from `query_radius` and `S` and can't be set on its own. Otherwise, add a config-time check that `cell_size * S >= query_radius`, in line with the project's fail-explicitly rule.

findings.title: "Correct neighborhood is preserved" is false once the cap applies
findings.description:
Subdivision keeps the same search area. But with `max_neighbors=32` and hundreds of candidates per cell, the cap picks neighbors by scan order. With S=1, the first 32 come from the (-1,-1) cell. With S=3, they come from the first sub-cells of the 7×7 block, starting at the (−3,−3) corner. These are often the far-corner cells, only partly inside the radius. So subdivision changes which neighbors are chosen, and that choice is biased toward one direction.

Slice 145 (lines 222–227) accepted the gap between first-k-found and true k-nearest, measured at population level. This slice changes the gap without discussing it. The parity check also runs at `mid-flock N=5000` (Step 5), where the cap may rarely bind. Two changes would close this:
- Correct the claim on line 56.
- Run the A4 parity check at a density where the cap binds (the gate workload), or document why the scan-order bias is acceptable.

findings.title: Relies on Quadrants supporting inner-loop `break`, with no check or fallback
findings.description: Slice 145 R1 (lines 363–368) listed "Quadrants may not support the conditional break in the inner loop" as a risk. Counter-gating was the fallback, and the shipped kernel uses it. This slice says the inner `for kk` loop accepts `break`, but gives no evidence. If the compiler rejects it, or turns it into predication that saves nothing, Intervention 1 fails. Add a small kernel test as the first implementation step. Also name the fallback: for example, a `while kk < end and k_found < k_max` loop, or relying on subdivision alone.

findings.title: Not specified how the `S` setting reaches the production engine (slice 146)
findings.description: `S` is added only to the "bench configuration" (line 50). Production runs will default to S=1. The A3 gate exists to show headroom "before slice 146 wires the GPU tick into the production engine" (line 116). That headroom is measured with S=3, which production won't get unless slice 146 knows to pass `S` through. The interface note says only that the setup/tick API is unchanged. State where `S` and the derived `cell_size` live in production config, or record it as a requirement handed to slice 146.

findings.title: Early exit sits in the caller, so A7 is no longer a one-place swap
findings.description: Option A puts the `break` in the kernel loop, outside `get_neighbors_first_k`. Distance-ranked k-nearest (the future A7 swap) has to scan every candidate. So that swap will need to remove the caller-side break as well as replace the seam. That conflicts with slice 145's A7 goal that the swap needs no kernel-structure change. This is acceptable, but say it in the A7 note on line 112.

findings.title: The upper bound on `S` is justified incorrectly
findings.description: At any `S`, a (2S+1)² grid of `query_radius/S` cells covers the same area. S=8 is not "larger than the physical neighborhood". Grid memory grows by S², which stays small at the stated world sizes. The real cost of a large `S` is the number of near-empty cells scanned per agent. The cap is fine, but rewrite the reason.

findings.title: Tier 2 NFR restated with specific targets
findings.description: The slice restates 60 TPS at N=50k on CUDA. It sets A3 at ≥100 TPS, and A2 and A4 match the plan's exit criteria (≥5× `force_total`, 20% statistical parity).

findings.title: Scope matches the plan entry, and module boundaries are respected
findings.description: Nothing changes in `TickResult`, the world server, or the numpy/numba backends. Both interventions stay inside the fused kernel and the bench config. Dependencies point only at slice 145. `S` is validated in Python at config time with an explicit error, not inside the kernel. The slice adds no new I/O or message paths, so it needs no failure-mode list.
